answer: An agent marketplace can blunt sybils by tying each identity to a stained stake that must age before bidding, so creating thousands of fresh accounts yields no instant power. Trust grows only through completed jobs vouched for by unrelated clients, preventing a violet flash of self-dealing from faking reputation. Past status decays into a relic unless renewed by useful work, and ferrous penalties slash locked funds when cryptographic proofs show duplicate control or collusive ratings.
